Absolute sensitivity selected layer 11 and tied magnitude exactly at perplexity 25.1388; no advantage was measured.

Candidates saved and reloaded, but no task quality gate, statistical uncertainty, inference speed comparison, or deployment benefit was established.
Implementation remains experimental in open PR #779, stacked on open PR #735; it is not integrated on main.

milestones.scope: Three 8,192-token WikiText-2 train-prefix, disjoint train-suffix and validation profiles for the pinned Qwen3.5-family model. Leave one profile out, aggregate the other two with mean-minmax, max-minmax and mean-rank, and compare each selected bottom-32 set to the held-out profile using 41 per-layer Jaccard scores.
research_questions: For this checkpoint and fixed cut, does mean-minmax aggregation of two calibration profiles improve the held-out profile bottom-expert-set agreement over single-profile selection?
acceptance_criteria: Run deterministic leave-one-profile-out analysis over all three pinned profiles; preserve hashes and per-fold Jaccards; report macro mean and worst fold against the single-profile baseline. A positive result applies only to these profiles and ranking metric.
milestones.remaining_work: Repeat with more independent profiles and additional checkpoints; then physically generate candidates and evaluate them on untouched task and deployment measures before using stability as an optimization objective.
limitations: Only three calibration profiles from one model were available; 41 layers are not independent samples, so no significance interval is claimed.
Mean-minmax improved the point estimates for both average held-out Jaccard (0.3129 to 0.3618) and worst held-out fold (0.2614 to 0.2736), but the gain is small and unreplicated.
This is ranking stability only. No candidate artifact, PPL, task quality, latency, memory, runtime, or recovery outcome was measured by this analysis.
The analysis utility is in open PR #738; no optimizer integration or production readiness is claimed.

history.reason: A reproducible leave-one-profile-out point-estimate improvement was found for the bounded Jaccard stability metric; it is not evidence of better model quality.
